runway.assumptions: Usable stock=calc: national reserve treated 100% usable (111d, post both 2026 releases, =146d pre-war minus 50d released) + private stock drawable down to reduced 55d legal floor only (81d actual Apr-26 minus 55d floor=26d usable) + joint remaining (~2d of the 7d facility after 5d drawn in Mar-26) = 139 usable days; converted to bbl at implied JP consumption rate 1.78mb/d (=8.5mn kL/30d release, x6.29 bbl/kL, cross-checked against 80mn bbl/45d Wikipedia figure). Shortfall=200kb/d assumes May-2026-like conditions (refinery runs back to 73.3% of capacity via alt-sourcing: US/Caspian/Latin America/non-sanctioned Russian crude), i.e. most of the Hormuz gap already substituted. NOT verified against a Sept-2026 hard import number -- this is the best-available proxy, dated May 2026.

Same 247mn bbl usable-stock base as above. Shortfall upper bound: ~70% of JP crude demand transits Hormuz per baseline reporting (95% of JP crude is Middle East-sourced, ~70% via Hormuz); after 2026-09-11 Saudi East-West Pipeline shutdown forces ALL Saudi crude back through Hormuz, and Hormuz transit is reported at only ~3% of pre-war levels -- i.e. near-total loss of the Hormuz-transiting share if no further substitution occurs. 0.70 x 1.78mb/d implied demand = 1.25mb/d. Treats the post-Sept-11 state as the operative 'current/full closure' scenario, since it is the LATEST baseline event (2 days before as-of date), not a hypothetical.

Same 247mn bbl usable-stock base. Lower bound of the post-Sept-11 severe scenario: assumes JP continues substituting most of the lost Hormuz volume with non-Gulf crude (as it did March-May, when >50% of supply was re-sourced away from Hormuz per METI's own May target statement), leaving a residual ~300kb/d unmet gap. Wide low-high range (300-1250kb/d) reflects genuine uncertainty -- no Sept-2026 hard JP crude-import or refinery-run figure was located in this search pass.

Same 247mn bbl usable-stock base. Illustrative recovery scenario: Hormuz transit partially restored (e.g. to ~50% of pre-war vessel counts) and East-West pipeline repaired, residual shortfall ~100kb/d. Included for completeness/sensitivity; not tied to any specific announced reopening as of 2026-09-14.

No mn-bbl usable-stock figure sourced. Qualitative finding only: Japanese petrochemical producers structurally hold only 'a few weeks' of naphtha feedstock; >40% of total naphtha supply is Hormuz-exposed (60% import share x 73.6% Middle East share, 2024 base). Multiple crackers were ALREADY cutting run rates by March-May 2026 -- i.e. naphtha is effectively already at/near its operating floor, ahead of crude. Treat floor_hit_date as 'already reached, ongoing' rather than a future date.

NOT a crude-style reserve: LNG cannot be stockpiled at scale and is continuously import-fed. usable_stock_mnbbl is a boe-equivalent conversion (2.3mn tonnes utility LNG stock x [51.6 MMBtu/t / 5.8 MMBtu/bbl] = ~20.5mn boe) shown ONLY for cross-product comparability -- NOT physically substitutable for crude. weeks_of_cover=2.5 is the commonly-cited normative range (~2-3 weeks) for Japanese utility LNG tank cover, NOT independently re-verified with a hard mid/late-2026 tonnage figure in this pass (Jan-26 and Apr-26 readings were ~2.3mn t, roughly flat). This is the scenario that applies ONLY if Hormuz-transiting LNG (chiefly Qatari cargoes) were cut to zero with no replacement spot purchases; as of Sept-2026 JERA describes stocks as 'sufficient' through October and the binding constraint is showing up as PRICE (JKM +118% y/y to $24.7/MMBtu on 2026-09-09) rather than physical shortage -- i.e. rationing-by-price is occurring before rationing-by-volume.

Usable stock=calc: 1,000mn bbl estimated commercial inventory (Project 54/Kpler/Vortexa est, China publishes no SPR/commercial data) x (1-0.25 tank-bottoms/minimum-operating-inventory floor, an industry rule-of-thumb assumption NOT China-specific-sourced) =750mn bbl usable. Shortfall=1.0mb/d per Vortexa/Kpler/Energy Aspects 'coming months' draw-rate estimate reported 2026-06-10 -- the most recent explicit draw-rate figure found. This is the LOWEST of the shortfall estimates in this table and is treated as the 'moderate/current' case.

Same 750mn bbl usable-commercial base. Shortfall=calc: 11.39mb/d (Feb-2026 baseline import rate, Kpler est) minus 7.2mb/d (Sept-2026 import rate, Kpler prelim) =4.19mb/d. This is a WIDER shortfall than the Bloomberg 1.0mb/d draw-rate estimate above because refiners have also CUT RUNS (demand-side adjustment) rather than fully offsetting the import gap from stocks alone -- the two estimates are not contradictory, they decompose the same gap differently (stock draw vs run cuts vs demand destruction already occurring). Included as the upper-shortfall / more conservative runway case.

Same 750mn bbl usable-commercial base. Shortfall=7.14mb/d = the May-2026 peak-stress gap actually observed (refinery runs 13.5mb/d vs imports 6.36mb/d, calc). Used as the 'full closure' stress-test analog since the 2026-09-11 East-West pipeline shutdown forcing all Saudi crude back through a Hormuz running at ~3% of normal plausibly reproduces May-like severity. If this rate were sustained, China's COMMERCIAL cushion alone (excluding the ~360mn bbl SPR) would reach its assumed 25%-of-capacity floor by ~late Dec 2026 / ~15 weeks from 2026-09-14.

Usable stock=750mn bbl commercial (as above) + 360mn bbl government/SPR (Project 54 est, assumed FULLY usable in a true national-security full-closure scenario, unlike the commercial floor assumption) =1,110mn bbl. Shortfall=7.14mb/d May-peak analog. Note: China has so far (through the searches in this pass) been reported tapping COMMERCIAL stocks, not announcing formal SPR releases -- so this row is a ceiling/backstop estimate, not an observed drawdown.

Same 750mn bbl usable-commercial base. Illustrative recovery scenario: partial Hormuz/pipeline restoration narrows the gap to ~0.5mb/d. Included for sensitivity; not tied to an announced reopening as of 2026-09-14.

NOT a runway figure -- no China gas SHORTFALL rate (kb/d-equivalent) or total consumption rate was sourced in this pass, so weeks_of_cover cannot be calculated; NA. usable_stock_mnbbl is a boe-equivalent conversion of the lower-bound 34bcm end-2024 underground working gas storage capacity (1 bcm ~= 6.1mn boe) shown only for cross-product comparability. Upper-bound 2025-26 plan target is ~55-60bcm (~336-366mn boe); one aggregator claims 67.45bcm already reached in 2026 but this conflicts with the more conservative plan figures and is flagged low-confidence. China's LNG-specific tank-inventory-in-days was NOT found (gap) -- China's gas security relies more on pipeline imports (Russia/Central Asia) and domestic production plus this storage buffer than on LNG tank days the way Japan does.

parameters._provenance_note: Every parameter carries a quality tag in `provenance`. `hard` = taken directly from a sourced research observation in data/raw/. `calc` = arithmetic on sourced observations, with the formula stated. `assumption` = a modelling judgement that could NOT be sourced in this session (the web-search budget was exhausted mid-research); these are the parameters to attack first when stress-testing the model, and they are listed together in `assumptions`.

baseline._comment: Pre-war reference levels (late Feb 2026), against which scenario prices are differenced.

cross_price._comment: Elasticity of each product price to a proportional Brent move, used when the sensitivity grid and the interactive controls scale prices off crude. Set to near-unity because in a chokepoint event the same physical constraint drives all four; they are assumptions, not estimated betas.

scenarios.label: De-escalation
scenarios.description: A shipping-protection accord or ceasefire restores roughly half of pre-war transit. Prices fall back but stay above pre-war on a persistent risk premium.

scenarios.label: Current grind (base)
scenarios.description: The state observed on 2026-09-14: transit at a small single-digit share of normal after the East-West pipeline shutdown, Brent above $100, price support still in force in both economies.

scenarios.label: Full closure
scenarios.description: Transit near zero and sustained, with Gulf loading infrastructure damaged. Substitution and reserve draw are both maxed out, so the residual must be rationed.

scenarios.label: Full closure, support withdrawn
scenarios.description: As full closure, but fiscal price support lapses under budget pressure. The retail price signal is restored, so more demand adjusts voluntarily and reserves last longer — at the cost of a much higher CPI print and a larger real-income hit.

JP.energy.lng_import_mt_yr.basis: Japan LNG imports ~66 mt in 2025 (65.87 mt FY2024). Confirms the value previously assumed.

JP.reserves.max_deliverable_draw_kbd.basis: Japan drew 70-100mn bbl between March and August 2026 - the largest drawdown in its history - implying a REALISED net draw of 0.75-1.1 mb/d. 900 kb/d sits inside that range, so the ceiling is now calibrated on observed behaviour rather than assumed outright. It remains a realised-rate proxy: the true engineering maximum is unpublished and may be higher.

JP.reserves.policy_max_draw_kbd.basis: Political willingness to draw; not published.

JP.mitigation.max_substitution_kbd.basis: Hormuz share fell 94.1% -> 59.3% by Jul 2026 (both sourced): (94.1-59.3)=34.8pp x 2,360 kb/d = 821 kb/d of demonstrated substitution. (Corrected from 826, which did not reproduce from this formula.)

JP.elasticities.oil_demand_price_elastic.basis: -0.05 short-run price elasticity of oil demand (EIA working paper, ws3_elasticities).

JP.elasticities.tot_transfer_to_gdp_mult.basis: Calibrated against GlobalData's 0.1-0.5pp per $10/bbl range for major net energy importers (0.3pp midpoint used as the Japan proxy; no Japan-specific figure found). Independently, Econbrowser/IMF compute Korea's transfer as 4ppt x 0.67 = 2.7ppt of GDP by the same method this model uses.

JP.elasticities.gdp_pp_per_pct_involunta.basis: 0.12pp of GDP per 1% forced cut in oil use. Now anchored in two directions. Upper bound: the electricity-curtailment literature puts market-equilibrium losses at under 0.05% to 2-4% of GDP (implying roughly 0.2-0.4 per 1% curtailment), with disequilibrium allocation quadrupling that — but electricity is an upper bound for oil, which is storable, substitutable and priority-allocated, so a value below that range is appropriate. Lower bound / total check: the IMF's April 2026 adverse scenario puts the regional GDP loss at almost 1pp, which the original 0.25 overshot three to four fold. Upgraded from `assumption` to `est`: still the least-evidenced parameter, but no longer an unanchored guess.

JP.cpi.energy_weight_pct.basis: CPI basket energy weight not sourced this session.

JP.cpi.retail_energy_passthrough.basis: Share of a wholesale energy move reaching retail prices.

JP.cpi.naphtha_to_cpi_beta.basis: Indirect pass-through via packaging, plastics and processed goods; no quantified coefficient could be sourced.

JP.policy.subsidy_passthrough_block.basis: Fraction of the retail price signal blocked by subsidy, which is what suppresses voluntary demand response.

JP.policy.gdp_support_pp.basis: Demand support from the fiscal package.

conversions.bcm_per_mt_lng.basis: 1.36 bcm per mt is the standard convention; not verified this session. Used to derive CN.energy.lng_import_mt_yr.

JP.cpi.oil_share_of_energy_basket.basis: Split of the CPI energy basket between oil-linked items (gasoline, kerosene) and gas/electricity. Introduced so the CPI channel responds to the LNG price move as well as Brent - previously it was driven by Brent alone, which understated the energy effect.

CN.cpi.oil_share_of_energy_basket.basis: Split of the CPI energy basket between oil-linked items (gasoline, kerosene) and gas/electricity. Introduced so the CPI channel responds to the LNG price move as well as Brent - previously it was driven by Brent alone, which understated the energy effect.

JP.lng.imports_via_hormuz_pct.basis: Japan sourced ~11% of LNG from Qatar+UAE pre-war (ws2_dependency).

CN.lng.imports_via_hormuz_pct.basis: China sourced ~30% of LNG imports from Qatar+UAE pre-war (ws2_dependency).

JP.lng.stock_mt.basis: METI weekly survey: utilities held 2.19mn t in March 2026, having RAISED stocks 10%. Stocks were 12.2% above the 2021-25 end-January average and 23% above a year earlier - they were not depleted.

JP.lng.stock_days_of_use.basis: METI/Reuters: 2.19mn t equals about 12 days of domestic use. Replaces the study's earlier 2-3 week estimate.

CN.lng.stock_mt.basis: China does not publish comparable utility LNG stocks. Left null; China's LNG runway is therefore not computed.

JP.lng.max_substitution_mt_yr.basis: Alternative LNG cargoes Japan could secure within a year (US, Australia, resales). Japan's Strategic Buffer LNG programme adds only ~0.84mt/yr, so this is dominated by commercial re-sourcing. Unsourced.

JP.lng.switchable_mt_yr.basis: Gas demand that can be met instead by coal, oil or restarted nuclear. Gas is 31-34% of Japan's generation and gas-to-coal switching is the one clearly price-induced demand response observed in the data, so this channel is real; its size is assumed.

CN.lng.switchable_mt_yr.basis: Large: gas is only 2.9% of Chinese generation and coal self-sufficiency exceeds 84%, so China's power sector is barely exposed to an LNG shortfall.

JP.cpi.gas_retail_passthrough.basis: Gas and electricity reach households through REGULATED, lagged tariffs and are directly subsidised, so a wholesale JKM move passes through far less than a pump-price move does. Calibrated so the base scenario reproduces Japan's realised position: core CPI 1.8% with subsidies holding about 1.0pp off implies roughly 2.8% ex-subsidy, which this value delivers. Using the oil pass-through for gas produced +4.7pp, which the realised data contradicts.

CN.cpi.gas_retail_passthrough.basis: Gas and electricity reach households through REGULATED, lagged tariffs and are directly subsidised, so a wholesale JKM move passes through far less than a pump-price move does. Calibrated so the base scenario reproduces Japan's realised position: core CPI 1.8% with subsidies holding about 1.0pp off implies roughly 2.8% ex-subsidy, which this value delivers. Using the oil pass-through for gas produced +4.7pp, which the realised data contradicts.

JP.naphtha.direct_import_me_pct.basis: Japan imports about 40% of its naphtha directly from the Middle East.

JP.naphtha.refinery_derived_share_pct.basis: Domestic refining supplies roughly another 40% of naphtha demand. Scaled in the model by the realised refinery run reduction rather than by Hormuz throughput, because the crude channel already determines how much crude arrives - applying throughput to both slices would double-count the same missing barrels.

JP.naphtha.refinery_crude_me_pct.basis: 95% of the crude used in Japanese refining was ME-sourced pre-war. Recorded for context: it sets the STRUCTURAL exposure (~78% of naphtha is ME-linked) but not the realised loss, since Japan re-sourced crude and kept runs at 67-77%.

JP.naphtha.stock_days.basis: Private naphtha inventory of 20 days. Reported by a trade site rather than a statistical agency, so downgraded from `hard`; it is load-bearing and deserves a primary-source check.

JP.naphtha.cracker_rate_prewar_pct.basis: April 2025 baseline = April 2026's record-low 67.3% plus the reported 11.3pp y/y decline.

JP.naphtha.max_substitution_pct.basis: CALIBRATED to April 2026: corrected gross loss is 39.3% of supply (36.0 direct + 3.3 refinery-derived), and the observed cracker decline was 11.3pp, so 28.0% of supply must have been re-sourced. UNDER-IDENTIFIED: one observation cannot separate this from the pass-through coefficient, which is fixed at 1.0 by assumption. The level therefore fits April by construction; the scenario variation is illustrative.

JP.naphtha.gap_to_cracker_passthrough.basis: Fixed at 1.0, the Leontief bound - a cracker cannot process feedstock it does not have. Below 1.0 would represent inventory draw and yield flexibility. Held fixed because one observation cannot identify both this and the substitution capacity.

JP.naphtha.downstream_buffer_days.basis: PE and PP inventories reported to cover three-plus months of demand. Trade-site source, so `est` not `hard`.

CN.naphtha.direct_import_me_pct.basis: Not sourced for China; left null so no Chinese naphtha result is produced.

CN.naphtha.refinery_derived_share_pct.basis: Not sourced for China; left null so no Chinese naphtha result is produced.

CN.naphtha.refinery_crude_me_pct.basis: Not sourced for China; left null so no Chinese naphtha result is produced.

CN.naphtha.stock_days.basis: Not sourced for China; left null so no Chinese naphtha result is produced.

CN.naphtha.cracker_rate_prewar_pct.basis: Not sourced for China; left null so no Chinese naphtha result is produced.

CN.naphtha.max_substitution_pct.basis: Not sourced for China; left null so no Chinese naphtha result is produced.

CN.naphtha.gap_to_cracker_passthrough.basis: Not sourced for China; left null so no Chinese naphtha result is produced.

CN.naphtha.downstream_buffer_days.basis: Not sourced for China; left null so no Chinese naphtha result is produced.

assumptions: Per-$10/bbl GDP elasticities could not be sourced for Japan or China; the GDP channel therefore runs off a measured income transfer times an assumed multiplier rather than a published elasticity.

Reserve deliverability ceilings are unpublished for both economies and are assumed. In most scenarios deliverability, not stock size, is what binds — so this assumption drives the runway more than the reserve totals do.
CPI energy weights, retail pass-through and the naphtha beta are assumed; only Japan's aggregate subsidy effect on CPI (-1.0 pp) is sourced.
Nominal GDP levels and Japan's oil demand and LNG tonnage are standard magnitudes, not figures verified against a source in this session.

Product prices are scaled off Brent with near-unity betas in the interactive grid; in reality naphtha and LPG have moved further than crude in this episode, so the grid understates the petrochemical channel.
China's reserve position rests on commercial estimates throughout, since no official data is published.
LNG conversion factors (52 mmbtu/t, 1.36 bcm/mt) are standard conventions, not sourced this session.
The LNG channel now models a physical balance and runway, but its substitution and fuel-switching capacities are assumed, and China's LNG stock is not published so no Chinese LNG runway is computed.
GDP is expressed in USD via fixed FX (USDJPY 150, USDCNY 7.0); a 10% FX error moves every %-of-GDP result by about 10%.

The CPI channel is calibrated so the base scenario reproduces Japan's realised core CPI (1.8%, about 2.8% ex-subsidy). Gas pass-through is set well below oil pass-through to reflect regulated, lagged utility tariffs. China's equivalent is not calibrated against a realised print.
China's naphtha exposure could not be sourced, so no Chinese naphtha result is computed.
The rationing coefficient (0.12) is bracketed by the electricity-curtailment literature above and the IMF scenario benchmark below, but no direct estimate for oil rationing exists.

The naphtha channel is UNDER-IDENTIFIED: one observation (April's 67.3% cracker rate) cannot separate substitution capacity from gap-to-cracker pass-through, so pass-through is fixed at 1.0 and substitution calibrated. Its level fits April by construction; treat scenario variation as illustrative.
Japan's naphtha stock (20 days) and polymer buffer (3 months) come from a trade site rather than a statistical agency and are load-bearing; both are tagged `est` pending a primary source.

fx._comment: Used only to express GDP in USD for the terms-of-trade ratio. A 10% FX error moves every %-of-GDP result by ~10%.
